source_name: Addiko Bank AG group investor relations (parent of Addiko Slovenia)
why_relevant: Addiko Slovenia is a subsidiary of Vienna-listed Addiko Bank AG; group-level SREP requirements, Pillar 3 and regulatory-risk commentary are disclosed at parent level in English and often name Slovenian country impacts not published locally.

source_name: Banka Intesa Sanpaolo d.d. — Razkritja (Pillar 3) and annual reports
why_relevant: Koper-based systemic subsidiary of Intesa Sanpaolo. Publishes 'Razkritja' as a standalone document per Part Eight of Reg. 575/2013 plus full annual reports — a stable multi-year series (2017-2024 observed) with regulatory-compliance and risk sections.

source_name: Gorenjska banka — Letna poročila in razkritja dodatnih informacij
why_relevant: AIK Banka-owned Slovenian bank publishing quarterly-dated Pillar 3 disclosures (31.3 / 30.6 / 30.9 / 31.12) — one of the few Slovenian banks with a genuinely quarterly regulatory-disclosure cadence, useful for detecting capital/requirement shifts between annual cycles.

source_name: Delavska hranilnica — Obvestila (public announcements)
why_relevant: DH is the largest domestically-owned savings bank and a fast retail-payments innovator. Its 'obvestila' stream carries public announcements, AGM notices, report-publication notices and customer notices — a good proxy for how a smaller ZBS-member institution absorbs regulatory deadlines.

source_name: Delavska hranilnica — Za vlagatelje / javne objave in letna poročila
why_relevant: Investor-facing mirror holding annual reports and 'razkritja dodatnih informacij o poslovanju' — the Pillar 3 equivalent for this institution.

source_name: UniCredit Banka Slovenija — customer notices on payment operations
why_relevant: Payment-cut-off and payment-scheme notices are where SEPA/instant-payments regulatory deadlines become concretely observable at the product level. UniCredit SI was not in the original cell list but is a systemic private bank in the same demand-side category.

source_name: UniCredit Developer Portal — Slovenia PSD2/instant-payments API newsroom
why_relevant: Bank developer portals reveal PSD2/instant-payments compliance timing at a technical level (sandbox availability, API version deadlines) months before customer-facing notices — an early-warning channel for payment regulation implementation in SI.

source_name: Banka Sparkasse d.d. — instant payments / payment services product pages
why_relevant: Steiermärkische-owned Slovenian bank; product pages document how the Instant Payments Regulation (9 Oct 2025) and Verification of Payee obligations were implemented commercially. Useful comparative datapoint against NLB/OTP.

source_name: Društvo Mali delničarji Slovenije (MDS) — bank shareholder pages
why_relevant: Minority-shareholder association aggregating AGM materials, squeeze-outs and disclosure disputes for essentially every Slovenian bank (NLB, Gorenjska, Addiko, SKB, BKS, DBS, Intesa, DH, Hranilnica LON, KD Banka, SID, UniCredit). Reveals contested or delayed disclosures that banks' own IR pages present neutrally.

source_name: OTP Group Slovenia annual report 2024 (third-party mirror)
why_relevant: Mirrors of bank annual reports on third-party sites (sustainability/media portals) provide fallback access when bank sites reorganise their opaque fileid-based download URLs. Confirms the 2024 report restates 2023 as if NKBM and SKB had operated combined.

source_name: Forbes Slovenija / N1 — banking regulatory and merger reporting
why_relevant: Business media surfaces bank disclosures that are otherwise buried in PDFs (merger effects, capital decisions, supervisory pressure) and often quotes management on regulatory-change impact — a discovery layer for which disclosures to pull.

source_name: Addiko Slovenia PSD2 / open banking explainer (Kaj prinaša PSD2?)
why_relevant: Bank-authored explainers of payment regulation ('Kaj prinaša PSD2?') document how the bank interprets and operationalises EU payment rules, and are typically updated when PSD3/PSR or VoP obligations land — an interpretive-layer source distinct from formal disclosures.

source_name: Združenje bank Slovenije – GIZ (ZBS / Bank Association of Slovenia), main site
why_relevant: The single most important Slovenian banking self-regulatory/industry body. Aggregates member-bank positions, coordinates comments on national draft laws (e.g. the 2025/2026 draft act on accessibility and use of payment instruments / cash and free basic payment account package), runs the sector's training calendar and self-regulatory codes.

source_name: ZBS – Organiziranost (committee / working-group structure)
why_relevant: Maps the ZBS committee architecture (Odbor za plačilni promet, Odbor za kartično poslovanje, Odbor za skladnost poslovanja, Odbor za preprečevanje pranja denarja, Odbor za pravna vprašanja, Odbor za informacijsko varnost, Odbor za informatiko). Each committee is a pointer to named bank experts, workstreams and the regulatory files the sector is actually working on.

source_name: ZBS – Smernice (self-regulatory guidelines)
why_relevant: Sector self-regulation: guidelines the member banks adopt collectively, often the Slovenian operational translation of EU/EBA requirements. Useful for tracking how a regulatory deadline is being implemented in practice.

source_name: ZBS – Kodeks (code of banking conduct / good business practice)
why_relevant: Formal self-regulatory instrument binding member banks; changes to it usually follow or pre-empt regulatory pressure (consumer protection, fees, cash access).

source_name: ZBS Izobraževalni center – Napovednik izobraževalnih programov / Terminski plan (training calendar)
why_relevant: Training titles and dates are a leading indicator of which regulations banks must be ready for and by when (DORA, MiCA, PSD3/PSR, AML package, CRR3). Seminar agendas often state implementation deadlines explicitly.

source_name: ZBS – Programi za prijavo (training registration portal)
why_relevant: Structured per-programme pages (agenda, target audience, dates) — usually richer and more machine-readable than the marketing calendar page.

source_name: ZBS – Članice (member list of Slovenian banks and savings banks)
why_relevant: Canonical, association-maintained roster of Slovenian banks, savings banks and branches of foreign banks — the firm-level pointer set for the whole SI banking cell, and a cross-check against the Banka Slovenije register.

source_name: Bančni vestnik (ZBS banking journal)
why_relevant: Long-running association-published professional journal; carries analytical articles by bank and supervisor staff on incoming regulation, often the most detailed Slovenian-language commentary available on implementation timing.

source_name: ZBS Annual Report series (Letno poročilo)
why_relevant: Annual reports enumerate which legislative files the association worked on, which committees met, and which consultations it responded to during the year — an authoritative retrospective index of regulatory activity.

source_name: EBA consultation response repository – Bank Association of Slovenia submissions
why_relevant: ZBS files formal comment letters to EBA consultations (confirmed examples: CP50, and comments on the Guidelines on loan origination and monitoring, Sep 2019). These are the association's most explicit, citable regulatory positions and reveal member-bank pain points.

source_name: European Banking Federation – Slovenia country page (ZBS as national member)
why_relevant: Confirms ZBS's EBF membership and gives a stable English-language profile plus contact/leadership pointers; EBF positions are the umbrella under which ZBS often aligns, so EBF position papers are a proxy for the SI association line.

source_name: Gospodarska zbornica Slovenije (GZS) – Sekcije / branch associations index
why_relevant: Master index of GZS branch chambers and sections; the route to the finance-adjacent and digital bodies (accounting services chamber, insurance brokers association, IT & telecoms association, cybersecurity section). GZS is a standard consultee on business-affecting draft legislation.

source_name: GZS – Združenje za informatiko in telekomunikacije (ZIT)
why_relevant: The GZS body that speaks for IT/technology vendors, including those supplying banking and payment infrastructure. Comments on digital, e-invoicing, AI and cyber regulation; publishes 'Koristni dokumenti' including reference price lists useful for vendor-market context.

source_name: GZS – Sekcija za kibernetsko varnost (Cybersecurity Section)
why_relevant: Industry forum on NIS2 / cyber-resilience implementation in Slovenia; relevant to DORA-adjacent obligations on financial entities and their ICT providers, and typically announces compliance deadlines to members.

source_name: GZS – Zbornica računovodskih servisov (Accounting Services Chamber)
why_relevant: Aggregates the profession most exposed to payment/e-invoicing/tax-reporting rule changes; issues member circulars on new obligations and effective dates, often earlier and more concretely than banks do.
